newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel surges against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel surges against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel surged one percent against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday but dealers said the market is expected to remain nervous and volatile.
"The session opened with a strengthening of the shekel and the trend gained momentum towards the end of the trading day," said a dealer at the First International Bank of Israel.
"Despite that, trading continues to be very nervous and spreads are still wide," he said.

The shekel plunged five percent last week after the cabinet announced a reform of the exchange rate regime and the Bank of Israel lowered the base rate by a sharp 1.2 percentage points to 12.7 percent.
A dealer at American-Israel Bank added that the shekel's rebound, which began on Monday, might be due to profit-taking. "The shekel nosedived last week and today investors were taking profits."
"The dollar failed to break the 3.6 shekels barrier and now it seems that the market will stabilise at the current level. The shekel might even continue to rise slightly in the coming days," he said.

But the FIBI dealer stressed that the market is still very volatile. "Its hard to predict where the market is going. We thought that the dollar would stabilise at 3.57 but it continued to decline. In the near term trading will continue to be very nervous," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5490 shekels against 3.5870 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8493 against 3.8916 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0870 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.1330 on Monday, and against the mark at 2.0348 shekels compared with 2.0569 on Monday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5400 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
